name: Possible Inverted Channel
why_habitability: The canyon floor west of and about 150 m below this stop holds a sinuous, raised ridge that the HiRISE team interprets as a possible inverted channel deposit. Inverted channels form when stream sediment is cemented in place by minerals deposited from water, and the softer rock around it later erodes away. Samples of the ridge could test whether liquid water once flowed here.
notes: Caption by B. Thomson (HiRISE, 2008): 'may be an inverted channel deposit'. Stop height above the floor measured from the DTM.

name: East Wall Layers
why_habitability: This stop is on the eastern side of the canyon, about 160 m above its floor. Gale crater's central mound is built of layered (stratified) material, and the canyon cuts through it, exposing the layers in its walls; sampling layer by layer gives an ordered record of how these deposits built up. The HiRISE team notes the canyon may have been carved by running water.
notes: Same HiRISE caption; PSP_007501_1750 is its stereo pair (no caption text). Height above the floor measured from the DTM.

name: Debris Deposits
why_habitability: The canyon holds debris deposits and levees left by past mass movements. Hughes et al. (2020) find the slopes too low for dry flows, which suggests water was needed to set them moving, likely groundwater seeping out of the slopes. Orbital CRISM spectra indicate the debris is made of polyhydrated (water-bearing) sulfates.
notes: Hughes et al., LPSC 2020 #2426. The abstract's 'Grand Canyon' on the SW flank of Mount Sharp is matched to this canyon by location; the source does not name this DTM. Not checked: which deposits are visible from this stop.

name: Sulfate Strata and Alcoves
why_habitability: The canyon cuts through sulfate-bearing strata, with tributary alcoves on its walls and coarse debris along its floor. Hughes et al. (2019) state that how much water was involved in forming these deposits is still unknown, which makes them a direct target for observation on the ground.
notes: Hughes et al., LPSC 2019 #3196. The abstract's 'Grand Canyon' on the SW flank of Mount Sharp is matched to this canyon by location; the source does not name this DTM. Not checked: which deposits are visible from this stop.

name: Northern Canyon Terrace
why_habitability: The walk ends on terrace ground at the northern end of the route. The layered rock of Gale's central mound is exposed in the canyon walls, and the HiRISE team notes the canyon may have been carved by running water.
notes: Valley name in this area per the IAU gazetteer: Sakarya Vallis, after a river in Turkiye (https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/15941); matched by location.
